title: Deep and narrow CO absorption revealing molecular clouds in the Hydra-A brightest cluster galaxy
question: Are there cold molecular gas clouds along the line of sight to the Hydra-A mm-continuum core, and what are their kinematics, temperature and column densities (as a test of chaotic cold accretion)?

what.value: HI absorption profile toward core (VLBA) compared with CO

evidence.quote: warmer atomic gas has also been detected in Hydra-A with the *Very Long Baseline Array* (VLBA) telescope (cite: Taylor1996).
They find a value of $N_{ \textnormal{H}_{2}} = 3.5\pm 0.3 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$

evidence.loc: 5 Molecular Gas Mass of the Disc
evidence.quote: $M_{\text{mol}}=2.26 \pm 0.29\times 10^{9}$ $M_{\odot}$ found from *Institut de RadioAstronomie Millimétrique* (IRAM) 30m observations

recipe.goal: Make moment maps and disc kinematics
recipe.method: Integrated brightness, velocity and dispersion maps of CO(2-1) with immoments
Bolatto2013 relation; Monte Carlo of 100000 noise-perturbed spectra, double-Gaussian chi2 fit to get SCOdv
key_parameters: F21 = 3.2, F10 = 1; rms from line-free range outside -600 to +600 km/s

recipe.goal: Remove emission and fit absorption features
recipe.method: Fit and subtract a Gaussian emission line excluding absorption channels (about -48 to -1 km/s), then triple-Gaussian fit via Monte Carlo
key_parameters: Mask limits scanned between -55±10 and +5±10 km/s; choose lowest reduced chi2 of flat-line fit
assumptions: Filling factor of 1 (lower limit on tau); tau_a = ln(I0/Iobs) equals tau

recipe.method: Ratio of velocity-integrated tau of CO(2-1) and CO(1-0) for optically thin LTE gas, solved numerically with Monte Carlo; then N_CO and N_H2
key_parameters: Spectra from larger circle matching CO(1-0) beam; single Gaussian fit per line
assumptions: CO/H2 = 3.2e-4 (Milky Way gas-phase carbon, all in CO); optically thin LTE

evidence.loc: 5 Molecular Gas Mass of the Disc
evidence.quote: we find an estimated mass of $M_{\text{mol}}=1.06^{+0.02}_{-0.02}\times 10^{9}$ $\text{M}_{\odot}$

evidence.loc: 5 Molecular Gas Mass of the Disc

answer_key.quantity: Peak CO(2-1) optical depth, region A

evidence.quote: find a cloud excitation temperature of $T_\textnormal{ex} = 42^{+25}_{-11}$ K

evidence.loc: 4 Dynamics of the cold gas disc
evidence.quote: average line-of-sight velocity gradient of ${\sim}$140 km s$^{-1}$ kpc$^{-1}$
